propositions: Acceptance criteria restating generic mechanical gates (e.g. 'all tests pass', 'plan review passes', 'children closed') add no signal to completion verifiers and mask ticket-specific deliverables.

No existing criterion discriminates between ticket-agnostic process gates (children-closed, CI/build/lint/tests pass, plan-review/verifier passes, merged/landed, DCO) and ticket-specific deliverable ACs.

A new 1-TURN LLM criterion ac-process-gate must fire when an AC's entire completion predicate is a generic mechanical gate (litmus: would this AC read identically on an arbitrary unrelated ticket?), and pass when the AC names this ticket's specific deliverable.

The ac-process-gate criterion is advisory, 1-TURN, not codebase-grounded, routed in ac-text-quality facet at container+leaf scope, with a checklist distinguishing not-applicable (no ACs present) from judgment keys per AC.

The implementation adds a rubric prompt, routing entry, registry membership, guide regeneration, eval spec with fire/no-fire corpus, and deterministic unit tests validating registration, routing, front-matter, guide parity, and eval shape.

Live bounded-sanity eval (kappa=1.0, recall=1.0, false_accept=0.0) confirms the criterion fires on process-gate ACs and passes on deliverable ACs; collateral changes fix singleton-chunk packing in registry and remove stale hard-coded criterion counts from documentation.
